questions.question: What makes an object a Spring bean?
options: It is created and managed by the Spring container
It lives in the main package
questions.explanation: A bean is an ordinary object whose creation and life are handled by the IoC container.

questions.question: What is the default bean name of a class ReceptionDesk marked with a plain @Component?
questions.explanation: The default name is the class name with the first letter in lower case.

questions.question: A class PharmacyStore is marked @Component("pharmacy"). What does context.containsBean("pharmacyStore") return?
questions.explanation: The custom name replaces the default one, so the default name is not registered.

questions.question: context.getBean("receptionDesk") == context.getBean(ReceptionDesk.class) is evaluated for a default bean. What is the result?
options: true, because both return the one shared instance
false, because each call builds a new object
It depends on the JVM version
questions.explanation: Default scope is singleton, so every lookup returns the same object.

questions.question: A developer writes PharmacyStore store = new PharmacyStore(); and expects a @Transactional method on it to start a transaction. Why does it not work?
options: The object is not a bean, so Spring never wraps it
questions.explanation: Objects made with new are outside the container, so Spring adds no proxies or injection to them.
